reason: Quote states deleting a flow log stops new records and does not delete existing data; the context adds that you delete the data from the destination yourself.
Quote states typical delivery of about 5 minutes to CloudWatch Logs and about 10 minutes to S3, on a best effort basis with possible delays.
Quote lists CloudWatch Logs, S3 and Data Firehose as destinations; the document history row dates the Firehose destination September 8, 2022.
The example under Security group and network ACL rules gives exactly this setup and the ACCEPT and REJECT records, with statelessness as the reason.

The quote supports ecs-cluster-arn as a version 7 field for traffic from a running ECS task, but says nothing about EC2 instances or AWS Fargate; the page says some ECS fields are '-' when the capacity provider is Fargate.
Quote states same-account or different-account Firehose delivery streams and an IAM role in both source and destination accounts.
What's New quote states support for EC2 resource tags and next-hop interface metadata, removing manual correlation; the fields table lists next-hop-interface-id as version 11.
Quote states the aggregation interval is always 1 minute or less on Nitro-based instances regardless of the specified maximum.
Quote states flow log data is collected outside the traffic path and does not affect throughput or latency.
The two quotes, each followed by its NODATA or SKIPDATA example record, state no data recorded in the interval and records skipped when internal capacity is exceeded.
Quotes state flow logs do not capture all traffic, Amazon DNS traffic is not logged, and traffic to your own DNS server is logged.
All four traffic types in the claim appear as items in the not-logged list under Flow log limitations.
Quote states several minutes to begin collecting and publishing and no real-time log streams.
Quote introduces the list; the snapshot list (lines 29-36) includes Elastic Load Balancing, Amazon RDS, NAT gateways and Transit gateways.
Quote states the restriction word for word.
Quote states data goes to an existing bucket you specify; the next sentence says records are a series of log file objects.
Quote states the three resource levels and that each network interface in a subnet or VPC is monitored.
Quote, under 'To create a flow log, you specify', lists accepted, rejected or all traffic.
Quote under Pricing states vended log ingestion and archival charges apply when you publish flow logs.
Quote states instances in associated subnets use the gateway endpoint and others use the public service endpoint.
Quotes under the longest prefix match bullet state endpoint precedence in the current Region and the internet gateway for other Regions because prefix lists are Regional.
Pricing note states no data processing or hourly charges for gateway endpoints and that routing S3 traffic through one avoids the NAT gateway data processing charge.
Quote on the S3 gateway endpoints page states the three excluded access paths and the interface endpoint alternative at additional cost.
Quote and its bullet state S3 and DynamoDB routes can coexist but not multiple routes to the same service in one table.
Quote and context state you choose route tables, a prefix-list-to-vpce route is added automatically, and it cannot be deleted or modified explicitly.
Quote supports the claim and display, but the spoken value 'S3 and DynamoDB only' adds exclusivity the quote does not state.
Quotes define a gateway route table, give the middlebox interception example, and the main route table rules say it cannot be the main route table.
Quote states attaching is not enough and lists route, public IP and security group requirements.
Quote states horizontally scaled, redundant, highly available, IPv4 and IPv6, and no availability risks or bandwidth constraints.
Page quotes state the new pool-to-single-ENI routing and the previous behavior; the document history row linking that page is dated August 13, 2025.
Quotes support IPv4 and IPv6 traffic and NAT for IPv4 communication, but do not state that NAT is performed only for IPv4 (the word 'only' is not supported).
Quote states the VPC and subnet need an IPv6 CIDR block and the instance an IPv6 address from the subnet range.
Quote states no charge for an internet gateway but data transfer charges for EC2 instances that use it.
Quote and context support the private-only awareness and the one-to-one NAT in both directions, but the qualifier 'IPv6 is not translated' is not stated in the quote or context.
Quotes state attach and configure routing, and for IPv4 a public IPv4 address via auto-assign or Elastic IP.
Quote states the 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 route to the internet gateway ID makes the subnet public.
Quote states billing per hour provisioned in each Availability Zone and per GB processed.
Quotes state one subnet per Availability Zone, an endpoint network interface with a private IP from the subnet, and that it is requester-managed.
Quote states the security group rules control traffic to the endpoint network interface from resources in the VPC.

Quotes support both tiers, their scope, features and the $0.00027 hourly rate per active IP address, but the qualifier defining an active IP address (on a network interface attached to a resource) is not in the quotes or context.
